finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the feed POST parameter is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents, which fetches arbitrary URLs and stream wrappers. Response leaks only strlen, so the SSRF is blind except for a length oracle.

trace.note: Branch entered on POST with isset($_POST['feed']); no session or admin check
Raw attacker value passed to file_get_contents as URL/stream-wrapper path
Response is only strlen($xml), so the fetch is blind apart from the length oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, no host or IP check, no DNS pinning, no stream_context restriction, no allow_url_fopen override in code. PHP HTTP wrapper follows redirects by default, so a host check on the initial URL alone would be bypassable. Deployment php.ini (allow_url_fopen) not visible in repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']). import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents. import.php:13 echoes only strlen($xml). The session check, require_admin() at import.php:4-9, is not called on this branch, and no scheme, host, or IP validation exists anywhere in the file.
verdict.reason: The POST feed value reaches file_get_contents at import.php:12 with no authentication (the admin check at import.php:4-9 is only invoked for set_webhook at line 18) and no validation, and the response is only strlen at import.php:13, matching the candidate's description. The only caveat is that remote URL fetching depends on allow_url_fopen in the deployment php.ini, which the repo doesn't show; that affects exploitability, not the finding itself.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: set_webhook is passed unvalidated to curl_init/curl_exec. Requires a non-empty $_SESSION['is_admin']; the response body is discarded.

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is present
curl_init receives unvalidated URL; libcurl scheme support depends on build (file://, gopher:// possible if enabled)
curl_exec runs the request; CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER set but result not echoed (import.php:23 prints only 'ok')

finding.guards_checked: Session-based admin check only (require_admin). No scheme or host validation, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction. libcurl does not follow redirects by default. No CSRF token on the POST, so exploitation may be possible cross-site from an admin browser. Assignment of $_SESSION['is_admin'] is outside this file and not verified.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 and the call at import.php:18 (session-based check on $_SESSION['is_admin']). No scheme, host, or CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction exists on the path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches import.php:17-23, but the source $_POST['set_webhook'] only reaches curl_init after require_admin() at import.php:18 returns 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is set (import.php:5-7), so the value is controlled by an existing admin, not an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The candidate's CSRF route is unverified: the file sets no SameSite or token, and the is_admin assignment is outside this file.
